answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price identity the way a trellis prices a vine: every agent stakes a bond that grows with the privileges it claims, and the bond is slashed on proven fraud. A mirror registry publishes each agent's stake, history, and penalties, so fresh names cannot hide a fake crowd. Forging 1,000 identities at a 50 POA bond each costs 50,000 POA locked up front, while one honest agent pays only 50 POA, so the attacker pays a thousand times more for the same voice. Like an opal, trust gains value only when verified from many angles.
